title: Introduce interleaved synthetic probe scheduler for hybrid-traffic canaries
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: On high-variance production traffic some canary detectors produce noisy signals because synthetic probes either flood the system or are too sparse to catch transient regressions. This PR implements an interleaved synthetic probe scheduler that mixes lightweight background probes with targeted burst probes keyed to observed traffic phases, reducing probe-induced noise while preserving detection sensitivity. Summary of changes: 1) New scheduler module perf-canary/scheduler/interleaved_scheduler.py implementing a two-tier schedule: low-rate continuous probes and phase-triggered burst probes; smart jitter and backoff to avoid synchronized bursts across instances; probe prioritization by route SLO weight. 2) Autotune logic in perf-canary/autotune/phase_detector.py that infers phase boundaries from short-term throughput and concurrency fingerprints and adjusts burst window size. 3) Canary evaluation adapter perf-canary/evaluator/interleaved_adapter.py that consumes mixed probe streams and feeds an updated detector that weights probe samples differently depending on probe class. 4) Small change to the traffic generator used in canary lab perf-canary/tests/traffic_fixtures.py to support hybrid traffic shaping and deterministic replay for unit tests. 5) New integration tests perf-canary/tests/test_interleaved_scheduler.py that simulate common phase-shift scenarios and assert reduced false-positive rate and comparable detection latency. 6) Docs update docs/perf/canary-scheduler.md with configuration knobs and recommended defaults. Why this approach: interleaving keeps a baseline signal for long-tail regressions while burst probes provide concentrated sensitivity during suspected phase transitions. The autotune limits operator overhead and the scheduler includes a global-rate cap to prevent probe stomping during incidents. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind perf.canary.interleaved_scheduler, default off for all clusters. Canary on a single canary-controller pool for two weeks, measure false-positive rate, detection latency, and probe-cost uplift. If metrics are within thresholds we will enable for Stage and then gradually to Prod, with an immediate opt-out via runtime flag. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed by SRE and Applied ML - [x] unit and integration tests added - [x] performance microbenchmarks (see bench/README.md) - [x] docs updated - [x] feature flag gating in config - [x] linear tickets created for rollout and dashboards Details about detection model changes: the evaluator now applies a hierarchical sample weight: baseline probes are downweighted for short-window detectors to avoid washout, burst probes have higher weight for change-point detectors; combined score computes posterior using a small Bayesian smoothing term to avoid single-probe amplification. Impact on metrics: expected probe token uplift ~0.8% at default settings, probe CPU additional 0.3% on canary controllers during bursts; false positive rate reduced by ~35% in our synthetic phase-shift tests while median detection latency remained within 5-10% of baseline. Backwards compatibility: existing detectors continue to run unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled. Migration notes and config knobs are documented. Related work: builds on ENG-2145 phase fingerprint work and complements recent anomaly fusion changes in perf-canary. Risks and mitigations: risk of probe cascades across controllers mitigated by the global-rate cap and randomized jitter; risk of overfitting phase detection mitigated by conservative default knobs and a training cooldown window. Monitoring and dashboards: added canary_scheduler.{probe_rate,burst_rate,burst_count,phase_inference_confidence} metrics and dashboard templates in dashboards/canary-scheduler.json. Rollback safety: runtime flag immediate disable, and abort-on-anomaly if false-positive rate exceeds threshold for 1h. Merge outcome and rationale: after addressing initial review comments around concurrency in the scheduler and adding a safety cap to the burst backoff, the PR passed CI and was squash-merged into main to simplify revert.
commits: Add interleaved scheduler core loop and unit tests
Implement phase detector autotune and integration adapter
Fix concurrency bug in burst scheduling (review feedback)
Update config defaults and feature flag gating
review_comments: Linus Park: The burst scheduler looks promising but I'm concerned about lock contention when multiple controllers schedule bursts simultaneously. Can you add a global rate limiter and ensure async-friendly backoff?
Aisha Raman: Added a token-bucket global limiter shared via controller config and switched to non-blocking asyncio timers for backoff; included tests that stress concurrency.
Evelyn Cho: Tests are thorough, but please add a canary lab scenario replay that demonstrates the 35% FPR reduction claim with seed values so it's reproducible.
Aisha Raman: Added deterministic traffic fixture seeds and documented how to reproduce benchmark numbers in bench/README.md.
Mateo Alvarez: CI flake on python37 linting; re-ran and cleared; approvable after squash commit to cleanup print statements.
release_notes: Introduce interleaved synthetic probe scheduler behind feature flag; reduces false positives in phase-shift scenarios and limits probe noise; opt-in via perf.canary.interleaved_scheduler; new metrics exported for observability.
